categories.name: Identity & Accuracy
categories.question: Can a prospective customer confidently understand who this company is, where it operates, when it is available, and whether its public information is coherent?

categories.name: Relevance & Service Coverage
categories.question: Does the profile accurately communicate the services the business wants local customers to hire it for?

categories.name: Conversion & Actionability
categories.question: Can a ready-to-buy searcher take a useful next action with minimal friction?

categories.name: Reputation & Trust
categories.question: Does publicly observable reputation provide sufficient and current trust for a customer to act?

categories.name: Content & Freshness
categories.question: Does the profile visibly demonstrate an active, credible company performing the work it claims to perform?

categories.name: Handoff & Journey Continuity
categories.question: Does the customer journey remain coherent when the prospect leaves Google?

categories.name: Measurement & Attribution
categories.question: Can activity originating from the profile be meaningfully measured?

checks.title: Business status and identity
evidence: Places API: businessStatus=OPERATIONAL; displayName=Acme Plumbing matches the destination title.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Confirm the profile status and legal trading name, then correct any mismatch.

checks.title: Primary category fits the core business
evidence: Places API primaryType=plumber; destination H1 names plumbing repair and drain service. The category is specific and accurate.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Choose the most specific accurate primary category for the core service.

checks.title: Additional categories are relevant, not stuffed
evidence: Places API types include plumber, drainage service, and water heater repair. Drainage is supported by the site; water-heater evidence is thin, so the set is not fully supported.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Remove unsupported categories and keep only services with real delivery evidence.

checks.title: Primary phone is present and coherent
evidence: Places API nationalPhoneNumber and destination tel: action both show (555) 010-0200.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Use one tracked or primary number and keep it consistent on the profile and site.

checks.title: Website action is present and plausibly owned
evidence: Places API websiteUri points to https://acme-plumbing.example/, the synthetic owned domain used throughout this fixture.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Point the profile at the business's own primary domain.

checks.title: Location or service-area configuration is coherent
evidence: Public profile and configuration: service-area business, no storefront address, Example County service area. The hidden address is correct, not a defect.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Make the location or service-area configuration match how the business actually sells.

checks.title: Regular hours are present and coherent
evidence: Places API regularOpeningHours: Mon-Sat 07:00-19:00. The destination publishes the same window.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Publish accurate regular hours and mirror them on the site.

checks.title: Description is specific and accurate
evidence: Profile description names repairs, drain cleaning, and Example County, but does not state a customer outcome or differentiator.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Write a short description around services, customer, and service area.

checks.title: Relevant attributes support the buying decision
evidence: No service-specific attributes are visible on the public profile beyond the category labels. Financing and emergency attributes are absent.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add only attributes the business can verify and support.

checks.title: Major services are explicit
evidence: Profile service list names drain cleaning and water-heater repair; the destination also sells leak detection and repiping. One major line is missing from the profile.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Name the major services in the profile and keep them aligned with the site.

checks.title: Commercially important services are represented
evidence: The profile lists repair work but does not distinguish the highest-value repipe and water-heater jobs. Commercial priority is unclear.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Put the highest-value services first and make them easy to recognize.

checks.title: Emergency or urgent service is represented
evidence: Profile description states emergency plumbing service and the preferred call action is present. Urgent work is represented.
checks.recommendedIntervention: State emergency availability and connect it to one usable urgent action.

checks.title: Service descriptions are clear
evidence: Service descriptions repeat category labels; they do not explain the customer problem or the work included.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Write one clear sentence per major service: problem, work, outcome.

checks.title: Service organization is coherent
evidence: Services are grouped as drain cleaning and water heaters. The grouping is scannable, though leak detection is absent.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Group related services and remove duplicates.

checks.title: Profile services match the website offering
evidence: Destination offers leak detection and repiping; the profile lists neither. The core plumbing offer matches, but one material line does not.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Align the profile and site service lists, then remove stale services.

checks.title: Category-specific attributes add service context
evidence: No category-specific attribute explains emergency availability, financing, or service-area constraints.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add the category attributes that materially help a customer decide.

checks.title: Phone action is usable
evidence: Places API phone present and the destination uses a tel: link for the same synthetic number.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Publish one primary number and make it tappable everywhere.

checks.title: Website action is clear and labeled
evidence: Website action is labeled with the business name and points to the synthetic owned domain.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Use the business's primary website and a clear label.

checks.title: Booking or appointment action
evidence: No booking or appointment action is present on the profile. The destination has a contact form, but that is not a booking action.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add one direct booking action and make the destination relevant.

checks.title: Messaging action
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add one business-owned messaging path with a clear response expectation.

checks.title: Directions or location action
checks.recommendedIntervention: Provide a correct address and directions action.

checks.title: Mobile handoff is compatible
evidence: The destination is usable at mobile width, but its contact form sits below a large stock hero image. One extra scroll adds friction, not a dead end.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Make the first destination a mobile-usable page owned by the business.

checks.title: Emergency action pathway
evidence: Emergency service is named and the primary phone action is usable, so an urgent path exists.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Make one urgent action unmistakable.

checks.title: After-hours path when observable
evidence: The profile states no after-hours policy. The destination says “call us” but does not say whether anyone answers after 7pm.
checks.recommendedIntervention: State after-hours availability and connect it to one action.

checks.title: Preferred next action is clear
evidence: Call is the clearest action; website and estimate request are secondary. The profile does not label a booking path.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Choose one primary action per intent and let the others support it.

checks.title: Contact paths do not conflict
evidence: Phone and website actions point to the same synthetic business. No conflicting booking or messaging destination is present.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Remove stale numbers, domains, and booking destinations.

checks.title: Rating provides a credible baseline
evidence: Places API rating 4.6 across 38 reviews. This is above the synthetic local baseline for the example.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Investigate recurring causes of low ratings; do not chase a number.

checks.title: Review count provides enough context
evidence: 38 reviews is a plausible base for a service business of this synthetic age and category.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Build a consistent review-request process; never buy reviews.

checks.title: Recent reviews are present
evidence: The public review sample has no review newer than 2026-07-18. At the 2026-10-27 audit date, recent proof is weak.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Make review requests part of every completed job.

checks.title: Review velocity is consistent
evidence: Review timestamps cluster in 2025 and early 2026, then stop. The sample does not show a steady recent cadence.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Use a repeatable post-job request instead of sporadic campaigns.

checks.title: Recent rating distribution does not signal a trust problem
evidence: One 2-star review in January 2026 cites a missed arrival window; the rest of the sample is positive. This is a small but relevant recent negative.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Read recent negatives, fix the recurring cause, and respond publicly where appropriate.

checks.title: Owner responses are present
evidence: No owner responses are visible in the public review sample, despite 38 published reviews.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Respond to reviews, especially recent negative ones, in a calm, specific voice.

checks.title: Owner responses are recent and relevant
evidence: No owner responses are visible in the public review sample, so no recent relevant response can be assessed.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Write short, specific replies that acknowledge the job and the customer's concern.

checks.title: Reviews contain service-specific proof
evidence: Two sampled reviews name drain cleaning and water-heater work. Service-specific proof exists but is not repeated across the sample.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Ask satisfied customers to mention the job and the result, without scripting a fake review.

checks.title: Profile imagery is present
evidence: Places API reports profile and cover media. A logo and cover image are present.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add a clear cover image and a recognizable profile image.

checks.title: Imagery is business-relevant
evidence: Two of six sampled images are stock graphics. The set is mixed rather than clearly business-specific.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Replace stock imagery with real, permissioned job and team photos.

checks.title: Useful job, team, vehicle, or before/after media
evidence: One job photo and one team photo are present; service variety is thin relative to the claimed services.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add captioned photos for each major service, including before/after where appropriate.

checks.title: Media is recent
evidence: Media metadata shows one recent upload. The rest of the set has no recent date or is undated.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Add a small number of recent job photos each month.

checks.title: Business-uploaded context is observable
evidence: Two images carry business attribution; the remaining images are user-contributed or unattributed.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Upload a small, current set of owner-provided photos.

checks.title: Recent posts or updates where applicable
checks.recommendedIntervention: Publish occasional job or service updates that help a customer, not filler.

checks.title: Website destination resolves over HTTPS
evidence: Destination fetch resolves over HTTPS with a valid certificate and no unrelated redirect.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Repair the destination and serve the site over HTTPS.

checks.title: Destination identity matches the profile
evidence: Destination title and logo match Acme Plumbing, but the footer uses a shortened brand name.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Align the business name, logo, and location across Google and the site.

checks.title: Phone, hours, and service signals stay consistent
evidence: Phone and hours match; the destination adds leak detection not present on the profile. One material service inconsistency.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Update the destination and profile from one source of truth.

checks.title: Booking destination resolves and belongs to the business
checks.recommendedIntervention: Repair or remove the booking action; use a branded, working destination.

checks.title: No obvious dead end at handoff
evidence: The destination has a contact form and phone link, but the first mobile viewport has no visible next action.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Keep one visible action on the destination that matches the profile promise.

checks.title: Source context is preserved at handoff
evidence: The profile website URL has no source parameter and the destination redirect preserves none.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Use a consistent, non-breaking source parameter on profile and booking links.

checks.title: Website action carries observable source context
evidence: No source or UTM parameter is observable on the profile website action.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Use one consistent source parameter that survives redirects.

checks.title: Booking action carries observable source context
checks.recommendedIntervention: Preserve source context through the booking redirect or form.

checks.title: Destination structure allows profile-origin measurement
evidence: Destination uses a stable root URL with no redirect chain that would strip query context.
checks.recommendedIntervention: Use stable landing URLs and avoid redirect chains that strip query context.

strongSignals.title: Commercially important services are represented
evidence: The profile lists repair work but does not distinguish the highest-value repipe and water-heater jobs. Commercial priority is unclear.
strongSignals.recommendedIntervention: Put the highest-value services first and make them easy to recognize.
strongSignals.fix: Prioritize the services the business most wants to sell.

strongSignals.title: Service descriptions are clear
evidence: Service descriptions repeat category labels; they do not explain the customer problem or the work included.
strongSignals.recommendedIntervention: Write one clear sentence per major service: problem, work, outcome.
strongSignals.fix: Write one clear problem-work-outcome sentence per service.

recommendations.title: Major services are explicit

recommendations.title: Phone, hours, and service signals stay consistent

recommendations.fix: Prioritize the services the business most wants to sell.

recommendations.title: Profile services match the website offering

recommendations.title: Relevant attributes support the buying decision

ownerDataRequired.title: Call answer rate
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: The profile can produce a call, but only the phone system can show whether it was answered.
questions: How many profile-origin calls were answered, missed, or abandoned?
What is the median ring time and voicemail rate during business hours?

ownerDataRequired.title: Speed to lead
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: Response time affects whether a ready customer books; public data cannot prove it.
questions: What is the median time from form, message, or missed call to first human contact?
Does the process change after hours?

ownerDataRequired.title: Booking conversion
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: A working booking link does not prove a booked job.
questions: What share of profile-origin booking attempts become scheduled jobs?
Where do customers abandon the booking flow?

ownerDataRequired.title: Review request operations
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: Public reviews show the result, not whether the request process is consistent or selective.
questions: Is every completed job asked for a review through the same process?
Who owns follow-up, and how are negative experiences handled before a request?

ownerDataRequired.title: Profile-origin revenue
ownerDataRequired.whyItMatters: Only authorized CRM and financial data can connect profile activity to booked revenue.
questions: Which jobs originated from the profile, and what revenue did they produce?
What is the close rate and average job value by profile-origin source?

journey.label: Identify
journey.customerQuestion: Is this the right business, in the right place, with a coherent public identity?

journey.label: Understand
journey.customerQuestion: Do I understand what this business does, where, when, and for whom?

journey.label: Trust
journey.customerQuestion: Does the public reputation and content give me enough confidence to act?

journey.label: Act
journey.customerQuestion: Can I take a useful next action with minimal friction?

journey.label: Handoff
journey.customerQuestion: Does the journey remain coherent when I leave Google?

journey.label: Response
journey.customerQuestion: What happens after I call or message, and how fast?

journey.label: Book
journey.customerQuestion: Does a booking request become a scheduled job?

journey.label: Customer
journey.customerQuestion: Which profile-origin customers became jobs, and what revenue did they produce?

journey.label: Review
journey.customerQuestion: Does every completed job feed a consistent review acquisition process?

journey.label: Measure
journey.customerQuestion: Can profile-origin activity be distinguished and measured?

opportunities.label: Financing
opportunities.why: High-ticket trades may lose ready customers who cannot pay the full amount up front.
opportunities.evidence: Only recommend when the trade and average job value make financing relevant.

opportunities.label: Maintenance plans or memberships
opportunities.why: Recurring service can increase customer lifetime value.
opportunities.evidence: A fit for HVAC, pest, plumbing, pool, and similar recurring needs; not a universal score requirement.

opportunities.label: Seasonal maintenance
opportunities.why: Seasonal service can create repeat demand without a new acquisition cost.
opportunities.evidence: Recommend when the trade has a seasonal maintenance cycle.

opportunities.label: Emergency routing
opportunities.why: Urgent customers need one unmistakable path.
opportunities.evidence: Only when the business actually accepts emergency work.

opportunities.label: Text/SMS path
opportunities.evidence: Only when the business can respond to texts.

opportunities.label: AI or after-hours reception
opportunities.why: Missed after-hours demand can be captured.
opportunities.evidence: An operational choice, never a score penalty.

opportunities.label: Online estimate requests
opportunities.why: Complex jobs may need a scoped estimate before booking.
opportunities.evidence: Recommend when the job mix requires photos or scope.

opportunities.label: Review request automation
opportunities.why: Consistent requests produce more current proof.
opportunities.evidence: Recommend when recency or velocity is weak.

opportunities.label: Missed-call recovery
opportunities.why: A missed call is a ready customer.
opportunities.evidence: Owner-data opportunity; never inferred from public data alone.

opportunities.label: Advanced attribution
opportunities.why: Profile-origin demand should be separable from other channels.
opportunities.evidence: Recommend when source context is absent or fragile.

opportunities.label: Video or job walkthrough
opportunities.why: Video can show work quality and team credibility.
opportunities.evidence: Optional; absence is not a universal penalty.

opportunities.label: Enhanced content cadence
opportunities.why: Useful updates and recent job media support trust.
opportunities.evidence: Optional; score content usefulness, not raw volume.

caps.label: The profile is marked permanently closed
caps.rationale: A permanently closed profile can stop nearly every customer action. This is the only status cap; temporary closure is a strong signal, not a punitive cap.

caps.label: No meaningful customer action path
caps.rationale: If a customer cannot call, visit the site, book, or use another action, the profile cannot complete its job.

caps.label: Major business-identity mismatch
caps.rationale: A material name, category, or destination mismatch makes every other identity signal unreliable. Caps Identity & Accuracy at 6/15.

caps.label: Broken primary website action
caps.rationale: A broken primary website handoff is a handoff failure. It caps Handoff & Journey Continuity at 4/10 and is not also applied as a Conversion cap.

caps.label: Dead booking destination presented as a primary action
caps.rationale: Advertising a dead booking destination is worse than not advertising booking. Caps Conversion & Actionability at 10/22.
